chunks: And this hadith was narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: We were narrated by Ja'far ibn Bashir and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from 'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
: (3) and he mentioned the hadith, except that he said: 'And each of them gives charity every day with two mudds of food.'

And this report is not contradictory to the hadiths that included giving one mudd of food or feeding a poor person, because this ruling varies according to the varying conditions of the obligated ones. So whoever is able to feed two mudds is obliged to do so, and whoever is only able to feed one mudd does that, and whoever cannot manage any of it bears no burden, according to what we have previously stated.
And to add clarification to this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْمُكَلَّفِينَ: The obligated ones (those subject to religious law)
key_terms.حَسَبَ مَا قَدَّمْنَا: According to what we have previously stated
key_terms.مُدَّيْنِ: Two mudds (a unit of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: How does the required charity for fasting vary based on a person's financial ability in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Alaa ibn Razin to demonstrate the principle of *takhassus* (specification) and flexibility in *kaffarah*, showing that the obligation scales with the individual's financial capacity (*istita'ah*). This resolves apparent contradictions in other hadiths by establishing a graduated system where the default is one mudd, but increases to two for those with greater means, while the completely indigent are exempt.
